title: Supreme Court orders Atibir Industries to pay Rs 125 crore more to settle assigned SBI debt
case_name: Atibir Industries Co. Ltd. v. State Bank of India and Another
card_summary: SBI had classified Atibir Industries as an NPA and assigned the debt to an asset reconstruction company for Rs 250 crore while Atibir's challenge was pending. The Supreme Court closed the dispute without ruling on the NPA tag or the assignment's validity, and instead ordered Atibir to pay Rs 125 crore more within 12 weeks as full and final settlement, with securities released on payment.
card_tip: A settlement route can close a loan dispute faster than fighting the NPA classification itself, but missed deadlines revive the original proceedings and forfeit the settlement's benefit.
verification_notes: Decision date, bench (CJI Surya Kant), citation 2026 INSC 1156, the Rs 125 crore figure and the 12-week/4-week deadlines are consistent across Verdictum, Law Trend and TaxGuru. Sources differ on whether the NPA/assignment validity questions were decided; the more detailed reports (Law Trend, Verdictum) agree the Court left those questions open and settled only the payment dispute, so the card reflects that reading.
